title: My First Bootstrap Grid
description: My very first hands-on intro to the Bootstrap grid system — building a multi-column responsive layout entirely with rows, columns, and breakpoint utilities.
skillsLearned: Bootstrap 5 grid (rows, columns, container), responsive breakpoints, the difference between fixed and fluid containers.
reflection: Coming from raw HTML/CSS, watching columns automatically stack on mobile was the moment the 12-column grid finally made sense to me.

title: Puppies — Bootstrap Image Gallery
description: A responsive puppy image gallery built entirely with Bootstrap's grid system — practice for arranging images cleanly across desktop, tablet, and mobile.
skillsLearned: Image-heavy responsive layouts, Bootstrap column nesting, alt text and accessibility basics, working with sandboxed cloud IDEs.
reflection: A small project, but the first time I actually thought about how a layout breaks at every screen size instead of just "how it looks on my laptop."

title: Summer-tainment Site
description: A multi-section summer-themed entertainment site exploring layout composition and themed visual design.
skillsLearned: Page sectioning with semantic HTML, color theory for themed sites, hand-written CSS layout.
reflection: A fun first attempt at giving a site a strong visual identity instead of just stacking content blocks.

title: Galileo Galilei Biography
description: An illustrated, multi-section biography site about Galileo Galilei — built to practice long-form content layout, typography hierarchy, and historical-themed visual design.
skillsLearned: Long-form content layout, typographic hierarchy, image-with-text composition, working with a themed color palette.
reflection: First project where I really cared about how the page felt to read — not just what was on it. Choosing fonts and spacing for legibility taught me design isn't optional.

title: Cute Spider
description: A pure CSS scene with a cute animated spider — exploring keyframe animations, transforms, and pseudo-elements to draw and move a character without images.
skillsLearned: CSS keyframes, transform-origin, animation timing, drawing with pure CSS shapes.
reflection: Realized how much expression you can get out of CSS alone — no JavaScript required to make something feel alive.

title: Spooky Ghost
description: A spooky Halloween-themed scene with a floating ghost and witch's cauldron, built from CSS animations and a sprinkle of JavaScript.
skillsLearned: Layered CSS animations, mood-driven design (color, motion, timing), scene composition.
reflection: Liked seeing how much atmosphere comes from slow, subtle motion. Restraint with animation made the scene feel polished instead of chaotic.

title: WordSalad
description: A randomized word-mixing toy — pulls from word lists and assembles silly phrases on demand.
skillsLearned: Arrays, random selection, basic DOM updates from JS.
reflection: Tiny but satisfying — proved that even a 30-line script can be entertaining if the data is fun.

title: Magic 8-Ball
description: A classic Magic 8-Ball recreated in the browser — click the ball, get an answer.
skillsLearned: Arrays, Math.random, event listeners, conditional rendering of text/images.
reflection: First time I built something where the interactivity actually felt physical — clicking the ball and waiting for an answer is its own little experience.

title: Name Generator
description: Generates random names from configurable first/last lists — with a clean instructional UI and footer.
skillsLearned: Splitting logic from presentation, combining arrays, writing small instructional UI.
reflection: Pushed me to think about what the *user* sees, not just what the code does — explaining how to use the tool mattered as much as building it.

title: Rock Paper Scissors
description: A full Rock-Paper-Scissors game vs the computer — running score, win/loss messaging, and a reset button.
skillsLearned: Game state, conditionals for game logic, score tracking, reset/cleanup patterns.
reflection: First project where I had to track state across rounds. A reset button sounds easy until you build it.

title: Postcard Generator
description: Build-your-own postcard — pick imagery, write a message, and see it composed live on the page.
skillsLearned: Form inputs, dynamic DOM updates, image swapping from JS, basic UX feedback.
reflection: Loved building something where the user's input directly shaped what they saw — that loop is what makes the web feel alive.

title: To-Do List
description: A working to-do list app — add tasks, mark them complete (styled only on the text, not the buttons), and remove them.
skillsLearned: Creating/removing DOM nodes from JS, event delegation, separating display state from data.
reflection: The rite-of-passage to-do app. The detail I'm proud of: completed styling applies only to the text, not the buttons — small choice, big polish difference.

title: Presidential Biography
description: A multi-page biography site with separate pages for biography, presidency, an interactive quiz, and a formatted works-cited page.
skillsLearned: Multi-page navigation, interactive quiz logic, properly formatted citations, site-wide styling consistency.
reflection: First project that felt like a real *site* instead of a single page. Keeping the styling consistent across four pages was harder than I expected.

title: Hangman
description: The classic Hangman game with health-indicator images that update as you guess wrong, plus sound effects.
skillsLearned: Game loops, win/lose conditions, image-state synchronization, integrating audio.
reflection: Adding sound effects taught me how much feedback shapes the *feel* of a game — even a tiny click sells the interaction.

title: Memory Game
description: A themed multi-page memory card-matching game — splash page, instructions page, and the actual game page, all sharing one design system.
skillsLearned: Multi-page game architecture, card flip/match state, themed image assets, separating CSS files per concern.
reflection: First time I designed a project as a *suite* of pages — splash → instructions → game. Treating it like a real product, not just an assignment, made it feel polished.

title: State Facts — Objects Practice
description: An interactive U.S. state facts viewer powered by JavaScript objects — pick a state, see its data rendered dynamically.
skillsLearned: Working with JS objects and object arrays, dynamic rendering from data, separating data files from view logic.
reflection: First time data lived in its own structure and the page read from it. After this, I never wanted to hard-code content again.

title: Team Roster Showcase
description: A multi-page team roster site with a home page, an about page, and a card-based roster page driven by JavaScript.
skillsLearned: Card-grid layout, multi-page navigation, JS-driven component cards, project documentation through code comments.
reflection: Pushed myself to actually write meaningful code comments here. Re-reading the project months later, I was glad I did.

title: Snowflake Designer Lab — Holiday Traditions
description: A group submission for the Winter Holiday & Traditions Web Design Challenge: an interactive snowflake-designer with 4/6/8-fold symmetry, 12 cultural pattern stamps, LocalStorage gallery, PNG export, and an animated snowfall UI.
skillsLearned: Cross-team collaboration on GitHub, React + TypeScript, Vue 3 widget integration, HTML5 Canvas drawing with live symmetry reflection, Tailwind CSS, LocalStorage persistence, Vite build tooling.
reflection: My most ambitious group build — and it was the project where version control and merging features into a coherent product became the real lesson. Easily one of the projects I'm proudest of.

title: College Recruitment
description: An interactive college-recruitment site — the first big senior project, blending content, custom styling, and JS-driven interactivity.
skillsLearned: Working on a fork-based collaborative repo, merge-conflict resolution, multi-screen interactive UX, custom theming.
reflection: The first project where I had to resolve real merge conflicts and pull from a shared upstream. Git stopped being a scary command-line ritual and started being a normal tool.

title: 1.01 — Functions Refresher
description: A short refresher project on JavaScript functions — declarations, expressions, parameters, and return values.
skillsLearned: Function declarations vs. expressions, parameters/arguments, return values, button-driven function calls.
reflection: Senior year started with a clean rebuild of fundamentals. Doing it again on purpose was the right call — I learned things I'd skimmed past the first time.

title: 1.02 — Arrays & Loops Refresher
description: Practice with arrays and looping patterns — iterate, transform, and render results into the DOM.
skillsLearned: for / forEach / map, array mutation vs. derivation, rendering arrays into HTML.
reflection: After this I stopped reaching for `for` loops out of habit and started picking the right tool — `map` for transforms, `forEach` for side effects.

title: 1.03 — Event Handling Refresher
description: Event-handling practice including a scroll progress bar — listening to user input and updating the page in response.
skillsLearned: addEventListener, scroll events, computed positions/percentages, throttling/rendering responsiveness.
reflection: The scroll progress bar was tiny but taught me how often the browser fires events. Performance-aware event handling clicked here.

title: AJAX Friends Project
description: A friends-card site that fetches data from a local JSON file via AJAX and renders styled cards dynamically.
skillsLearned: AJAX / fetch, async data flow, building DOM templates from JSON, separating data from UI.
reflection: First time a site of mine wasn't fully hard-coded — the data lived in its own JSON file and the page just read from it. That separation changed how I approached every project after.

title: Schedule Project
description: A Bootstrap-powered schedule viewer that pulls schedules out of JSON files and renders them dynamically.
skillsLearned: Bootstrap 5 components, fetch + render, JSON-driven views, header iconography and styling.
reflection: Combined two things I'd been learning separately — Bootstrap and fetching from JSON — into one project. That combination felt grown up.

title: Chang PhotoApp
description: A custom slideshow / photo gallery app built with jQuery and a custom JSON metadata file for each image.
skillsLearned: jQuery selectors and animations, JSON-driven image metadata, custom slideshow controls, separating image data from markup.
reflection: First real exposure to jQuery, but the bigger lesson was the metadata model — every image had its own structured record, not just a filename. That's still how I think about media-heavy sites.

title: Vue Mastery Tutorial
description: Worked through the Vue Mastery tutorial — building reactive components, props, computed properties, and basic Vue patterns from scratch.
skillsLearned: Vue 2 component options API, data/methods/computed, props, conditional rendering, event binding.
reflection: First reactive framework I'd touched. The mental shift from 'I update the DOM' to 'I update state and the DOM updates itself' was big.

title: Movie Poster Gallery
description: A Vue-powered movie poster gallery — load movies and metadata from JSON, render a custom-themed gallery of posters with no jQuery.
skillsLearned: Vue list rendering (v-for), JSON-driven content, custom theming with CSS, image asset management.
reflection: Applied the Vue tutorial to something that was actually mine — picking my favorite movies and theming the gallery around them. Made the framework feel personal, not academic.

title: The KeySpace Piano Studio
description: A full multi-page marketing site for a fictional piano studio — home, about, programs, and contact pages with a consistent visual identity and responsive layouts.
skillsLearned: Multi-page information architecture, brand-driven design (palette, type, imagery), consistent component patterns across pages, contact-page UX, accessible navigation.
reflection: The closest I've come to building a 'real' client website. Owning the brand decisions — palette, typography, voice — and carrying them across four pages was the most grown-up project I've done.

title: Journey Map Portfolio (This Site)
description: This portfolio: an interactive map of my three years in the program. Drive a car around a hand-illustrated SVG world, visit themed buildings, and pull project data from a JSON file with fetch.
skillsLearned: Vanilla JS architecture without frameworks, custom physics for the car, SVG illustration and parallax layers, WebAudio for engine + ambient sound, keyboard + touch input parity, JSON-driven content rendering.
reflection: The capstone — and the most fun. Every technique from three years had to come together: layout, animation, data, accessibility, sound. Making it feel like a *place* instead of a list was the hardest design call.

title: Little Bird Toys — Toy Company Site
description: A fully responsive e-commerce site for a fictional handcrafted wooden-toy company. Multi-page Bootstrap build with a product catalog, shopping cart with quantity controls, interactive components, and accessibility-first markup.
skillsLearned: Bootstrap 5 layout system, component-based CSS organization, JavaScript-driven cart state, multi-page navigation, semantic HTML + ARIA, responsive design across mobile/tablet/desktop, collaborative GitHub workflow.
reflection: A real multi-page product site — homepage, products, cart, about, and contact, all sharing one brand. Building the cart logic (add/remove, quantity updates, totals) was the first time I shipped state that actually felt like a real e-commerce app.

title: MHSToday — Student News Site
description: The Manalapan High School student news publication — a live, regularly updated newsroom site where I've contributed articles, photography, and digital storytelling across the school year.
skillsLearned: Writing for a real public audience, working inside an established CMS, headline + lede craft, digital photo handling, deadlines and editorial workflow, the difference between personal projects and contributing to a live shared site.
reflection: My first time publishing on a site I don't own. Working inside an existing CMS — with editors, deadlines, and a real readership — taught me that shipping reliably matters more than reinventing the layout for every piece.
